newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton closes lower following key USDA data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton closes lower following key USDA data.

text.p: NYCE cotton settled slightly weaker as the U.S. Department of Agriculture's long-awaited planted area estimate failed to inspire a more substantial price move, dealers said.
The USDA said growers would plant 14.0 million acres of cotton in 1997, compared with an estimate of 14.485 million acres in March. Analysts had pegged today's forecast at 13.83-14.30 million acres.
Market sources said last week's rally to a 15-week high of 77.65 cents in December reflected expecations for a reduction from the previous estimate, to around 14.0 million acres.

"The report was not enough for the funds to start running," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co, Inc, said. "They may be more inclined to do that when they see how long they are tomorrow."

NYCE will issue its weekly spec/hedge report on Tuesday. Johnson said a net speculative long position closer to 25 percent than 15 percent, could prompt liquidation and send December towards its downside target of 76.10 cents.
The benchmark contract closed down 0.28 cent at 77.12 cents per lb, having ranged from 77.39 to 76.75 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.18 lower to 0.05 cent firmer.
Resistance in December remained at 77.70-77.95 cents.
An estimated 7,500 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Friday's official 11,063 lots.
NYCE will be closed Friday for the Fourth of July holiday, and will reopen on Monday, July 7.
